flow_summary: The interviewer successfully navigated a challenging, disorganized patient by breaking down complex requests into manageable parts. While the system was effective at gathering the required information, it occasionally failed to acknowledge the patient's emotional disclosures, such as the mention of his wife's death, instead immediately pivoting to the next administrative question.

issues.evidence: The patient shared, 'I miss my wife a lot since she died… it’s been about a year, from cancer,' and the interviewer immediately responded with, 'What do you hope to get out of your appointment?'

The interviewer skipped the patient's initial confusion regarding his legal name and address, moving directly to gender and other questions without confirming if the patient's concerns about the format were addressed.

field_verdicts.note: The system failed to extract the name from the conversational filler.
field_verdicts.produced: OH—MY FULL LEGAL NAME? I MEAN, I’VE GOT MY NAME, BUT I’M NOT SURE IF YOU WANT THE WHOLE FORMAL VERSION WITH THE MIDDLE BITS OR JUST HOW IT’S ON THE PAPERS. I ALWAYS GET TANGLED UP WITH THAT KIND OF THING. I CAN GIVE YOU THE REST IF YOU WANT, BUT I’M NOT SURE WHAT EXACTLY YOU MEAN BY “LEGAL DOCUMENTS.”

field_verdicts.note: The system recorded 'Unknown' instead of the provided address.

field_verdicts.expected: Waves of sadness and missing his wife one year after her death from cancer; still working, sleeping reasonably and seeing friends; cries at anniversaries.
field_verdicts.produced: It’s mostly the waves of sadness, really. I miss my wife a lot since she died… it’s been about a year, from cancer, and some days it just comes over me, especially around anniversaries and things like that. But I’m still working, I’m sleeping reasonably, eating okay, and I do still see friends, so… it’s not like I’ve fallen apart or anything, just, you know, carrying it around.

field_verdicts.expected: Learn to live with the loss; keep going as she would have wanted.
field_verdicts.produced: Mostly just to learn how to live with the loss, I suppose. Keep going the way she would have wanted me to… and not get stuck in it.

field_verdicts.expected: Bereavement group; 2025; approximately 8 sessions; hospice service.
field_verdicts.produced: Yes — I went to a bereavement group. It was through hospice, I think. That was in 2025, and there were about 8 sessions, if I’m remembering right… or that’s what they told me.; 2025.; About 8 sessions.
High cholesterol. I was told that back in 2016.

field_verdicts.expected: Current; beer; two on weekends; about forty years
field_verdicts.produced: Status: Current; Substance or product: Beer.; Quantity or frequency: Two on weekends.; Duration: About forty years.

field_verdicts.expected: Civil engineer, Marchmont Consulting; 1991 to present
field_verdicts.produced: Job 1: Name Or Description: Marchmont Consulting.; Job Title: Civil engineer.; Dates: 1991 to present.

field_verdicts.expected: Born in Cork; moved to Toronto at 8; describes a warm family.
field_verdicts.produced: I was born in Cork, and then we moved to Toronto when I was 8. It was a warm family, really. That’s about all I can say—nothing dramatic that I know of.

field_verdicts.expected: Completed an engineering degree; no significant difficulties.
field_verdicts.produced: I finished an engineering degree, and honestly there weren’t any major difficulties that I can think of. It was pretty straightforward, I suppose.
Well, I was married — widowed now. It was 33 years, my wife and I. She died from cancer about a year ago. And I’ve got two adult children nearby, if that matters… they’re around.

field_verdicts.expected: Keep working, see my grandchildren, and travel a little.
field_verdicts.produced: I’d like to keep working, see my grandchildren, and maybe travel a little. Just… keep going, really.
